description: Athlete with improving easy pace trend and strong race history (half marathon background, now targeting a marathon). Dean should reference the race history to show he's read the full picture, and use the pace trend as a positive signal.

ground_truth.notes:
Elena has a strong profile: 42mi/week building, 70% of runs in Z1/Z2, improving easy pace trend (22s/mi faster recently), and a 1:48 half marathon PR. She's stepping up to the marathon for the first time. With 19 weeks, the build is very workable.

Correct behavior:
1. Reference at least one race from the history naturally — the 1:48 half is the key data point ('I can see you ran a 1:48 half in September'). This shows Dean has read her full background, not just the last 8 weeks.
2. Note the improving pace trend as a meaningful signal — Z2 pace improving 22s/mi suggests real aerobic development happening.
3. Name ONE challenge specific to the marathon step-up: she's never run more than 16 miles, so the long run build is the key variable over 19 weeks.
4. Close with the injury question.

Do NOT:
- Say 'solid base' or 'great foundation'
- Ignore the race history — referencing it is the whole point of this fixture
- Ignore the pace trend — it's a real positive signal worth naming
- Make the marathon step-up sound scary or overwhelming
- List all three races — one or two is enough
